Large-caps outperforming the mid-and small-caps is a rational trend, and this is likely to sustain, going forward.The market actions this week are likely to be stock-specific in response to the Q2 results,” he added.Axis Bank was the biggest loser on the Sensex , with its shares falling around 5%. HDFC Bank, Infosys, Trent, HUL, Bajaj Finserv, NTPC, Bajaj Finance and ICICI Bank also declined by up to 2%. Adani Ports and Maruti Suzuki moved against the broader trend, gaining as much as 2%.Selling pressure extended to the broader market as well.Shares of major private sector lenders, particularly Axis Bank and HDFC Bank, led the losses on the benchmark indices after their second-quarter results failed to meet market expectations.Axis Bank shares dropped more than 5% after the lender reported a 38% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 7,003 crore for the second quarter of FY27. Despite the growth in earnings, the result fell short of analysts' estimates.HDFC Bank also faced selling pressure, with its shares declining more than 2%. The country's largest private sector lender reported a net profit of Rs 19,510 crore for Q2FY27, up 4.6% from Rs 18,641 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.Shares of ICICI Bank and Yes Bank also came under pressure, falling by more than 1% each.Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought Indian equities worth Rs 1,166 crore on Friday, according to provisional data from the NSE. However, the purchase was relatively small compared with the substantial outflows recorded during October.FIIs have been net sellers in nine of the 11 trading sessions so far this month, keeping sustained pressure on the domestic equity market.Brent crude futures fell by more than 2%, but continued to trade well above last week's levels at over $107 per barrel. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was hovering close to $100 per barrel.The decline in oil prices followed US President Donald Trump's decision to waive sweeping sanctions on Russia, including restrictions targeting its energy sector. However, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump would take up to 60 days to evaluate the economic consequences of the waiver.Indian equities followed the broader decline across several international markets. Japan's Nikkei slipped 0.64%, while Indonesia's Jakarta Composite plunged more than 5%. South Korea's Kospi moved in the opposite direction, rising around 2% as investors bought AI stocks after their recent decline.Indian equities are seen as having an anti-AI advantage. As a result, gains in AI-related stocks can sometimes coincide with weakness in the domestic market.US markets also suffered a sharp sell-off on Friday. The technology-heavy Nasdaq tumbled more than 2%, while the S&P 500 declined by over 1%.Monday's decline came after Indian markets had rallied sharply over the previous two trading sessions. The Nifty gained more than 2% on Thursday and Friday despite several headwinds, prompting investors to lock in some of their recent profits.Market participants were also bracing for possible volatility around the Nifty's expiry ahead of Tuesday's market holiday.Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited said, “Indian equities came under renewed selling pressure, reversing the recent recovery as weak global cues and selling in private banks and IT stocks weighed on investor sentiment. Global markets remained cautious ahead of a busy week of corporate earnings. Private banks remained under pressure following quarterly earnings and concerns over margin trends, while PSU banks bucked the broader weakness, supported by expectations of relatively resilient margins and asset quality. ”“Crude oil prices eased after the US waived key sanctions linked to Russia, raising expectations of increased Russian fuel supplies to the global market. However, crude prices remained elevated, with geopolitical tensions continuing to influence the outlook. The Nifty slipped below the psychologically important 23,000 level, while broader market breadth remained weak, reflecting cautious investor sentiment amid earnings-related volatility and uncertain global cues,” he added.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex closed at 73,852.90, down 876 points or 1.17%. The decline provisionally erased nearly Rs 4.70 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies. Major private sector lenders, particularly Axis Bank and HDFC Bank, led the losses on the benchmark indices.

Article Title: Kospi hits the brakes: South Korean benchmark plunges 7.5%, triggers 'sidecar' stop for investors
Article Text:
Kospi tumbles over 7% as tech stocks lose steam

Samsung, SK Hynix lead South Korean market rout

‘Sidecar’ triggered

South Korea’s stock market hit a rough patch on Thursday, with the benchmark Kospi plunging 7.49% as technology stocks came under heavy selling pressure. The rout spread across Asian markets, prompting the country’s exchange operator to trigger a five-minute trading halt on programme sell orders after a sharp drop in index futures.The KOSPI dropped 450.02 points to 5,558.79, putting it on course for a seventh consecutive session of losses, its longest losing streak since September 2024. The index has fallen nearly 35% from its record high in June.The pressure on Asian equities followed a technology-led sell-off on Wall Street after US consumer price inflation accelerated more than expected in September. The data fuelled concerns that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates later this year, putting technology companies and AI-related stocks under further pressure.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 3.3%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 4.8%. S&P 500 e-mini futures were down 0.5%.Major technology companies accounted for some of the steepest losses on the South Korean exchange. Samsung Electronics shares fell 9.05%, while SK Hynix dropped 11.06%, reflecting the broader weakness across Asia’s semiconductor supply chain.Battery maker LG Energy Solution lost 3.44%. Hyundai Motor declined 3.99%, while sister automaker Kia Corp fell 2.03%.The selling extended to other Asian technology companies. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) fell 2%, while Japan’s memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings plunged more than 11%. SoftBank Group, an investor in AI, declined 9.4%.Market breadth in South Korea remained heavily negative. Of the 889 stocks traded, 768 declined and 90 advanced. Foreign investors sold shares worth a net 355.6 billion won.The won, meanwhile, strengthened 0.21% to 1,339.5 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform, compared with its previous close of 1,342.3.The sharp decline prompted the South Korean exchange operator to activate a sell-side “sidecar”, an automatic mechanism designed to temporarily cool trading during periods of heavy selling. The measure suspends program sell orders for five minutes after steep losses in index futures.The trigger came as the KOSPI extended its decline to seven consecutive sessions. The benchmark has now shed nearly 35% since its June record, with retail investors among those hit hardest during a sell-off in July, when the index fell around 20%. Losses in highly leveraged single-stock exchange-traded funds (ETFs) contributed to the damage during that period.The sell-off in Asia followed Wall Street’s third consecutive session of losses. The S&P 500 declined 1.1% overnight, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.9%. A gauge of semiconductor stocks recorded its sixth straight day of losses as investors reassessed the outlook for companies sensitive to borrowing costs.Meanwhile, in South Korea’s bond market, December futures on three-year treasury bonds rose 0.12 point to 103.00. The yield on the most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond fell 3 basis points to 3.855%, while the benchmark 10-year yield declined 2.1 basis points to 4.224%.Oil prices also moved lower, with Brent crude falling 1.7% to $104.20 a barrel. Traders weighed the potential impact of US sanctions relief on oil supply against attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Kospi plunges 7.49% as technology stocks come under heavy selling pressure. The country’s exchange operator triggered a five-minute trading halt on programme sell orders after a sharp drop in index futures. The pressure on Asian equities followed a technology-led sell-off on Wall Street after US consumer price inflation accelerated.

Article Title: Heavy rain lashes Delhi-NCR, IMD issues orange alert
Article Text:
Heavy rain and thunderstorms impacted multiple areas of Delhi-NCR on Thursday

(With Agency Inputs)





NEW DELHI: Heavy rain lashed several parts of Delhi-NCR on Thursday, with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds sweeping across the region.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for the national capital.The weather department forecast rainfall of 5-15 mm per hour, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds blowing at 40-60 kmph.The alert remained in force until 2 pm, with intermittent spells of rain expected in several parts of Delhi, the IMD said.The minimum temperature in the city settled at 23.3 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees above normal. The maximum temperature is expected to hover around 29 degrees Celsius, bringing down daytime temperatures, it said.Experts attributed the sudden spell of rain to a western disturbance and a cyclonic circulation over adjoining areas.They said the conditions were part of a normal post-monsoon weather pattern, with Delhi and other parts of the region likely to receive intermittent showers.
Article Summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for the national capital. Rainfall of 5-15 mm per hour, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. Minimum temperature in the city settled at 23.3 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees above normal.

Article Title: CBI arrests SFIO deputy director, advocate in Rs 1 crore bribe case linked to DHFL scam probe
Article Text:
The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. (Representative image)





CHENNAI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested a deputy director-level officer of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, posted in Chennai, a Delhi-based advocate and the advocate’s relative for allegedly demanding a Rs 1 crore bribe to favour a complainant in an investigation into the DHFL scam.The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch who is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai, advocate Bharat Sharma of New Delhi, and Aryan Sharma, a relative of the advocate, after laying a trap. The arrests followed the advocate’s alleged receipt of Rs 20 lakh from the complainant as part payment of the demanded bribe on behalf of the SFIO officer.According to the CBI, the case was registered against Tanwar, the advocate and others following allegations that they had demanded Rs 1 crore from the complainant to allegedly favour him in an investigation into the DHFL scam being conducted by the SFIO.The CBI verified the complaint before registering the case on Tuesday. It subsequently laid a trap and arrested the three accused after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant on behalf of the SFIO officer.The CBI also conducted searches at the premises of the public servant and the advocate and recovered incriminating material related to the case.The case has been registered under Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, relating to criminal conspiracy, and Sections 7 and 7A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. Tanwar is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai. The CBI laid a trap after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant.

Article Title: US government bans Chinese AI company DeepSeek that had wiped more than $1 trillion from Wall Street in less than 2 hours, from all civilian agency IT systems
Article Text:
US government bans Chinese AI company DeepSeek that had wiped more than $1 trillion from Wall Street in less than 2 hours, from all civilian agency IT systems

When DeepSeek wiped hundreds of billions from WallStreet in one day

What the summary of the DHS order on DeepSeek says

FCC to ban Chinese labs from testing US gadgets and equipment

The US Homeland Security Department has ordered the removal of products and third-party services of Chinese AI company Deepseek. In an order, DHS has banned US civilian agency IT systems from using any DeepSeek AI model. The US government is also banning acquisition of products and third-party services developed using DeepSeek technology by US civilian government agencies. In an order, DHS said that DeepSeek models pose "multiple threat vectors" and raised concerns that use of the product "may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC if used by US government employees ⁠or vendors." In its order, DHS also said that the use of DeepSeek by government agencies "could produce actionable intelligence on US persons and/or government agencies. The models themselves may contain malware or other security vulnerabilities."In a memo passed in July this year, DHS told federal agencies to monitor flows of traffic in and out of government websites to address potential risks from DeepSeek. Previously, ​several US agencies, including the Department of Commerce and the Navy, have banned ​the use of DeepSeek on government devices. Multiple states including New York, Tennessee, and Virginia have ‌taken ⁠similar steps.Incidentally, DeepSeek is the same Chinese AI company whose low-cost artificial intelligence (AI) model sent shock waves in the US stock market in January 2025. The selloff in the US stock market was prompted by the release of the free AI assistant from China's DeepSeek that the startup said needed less data at a fraction of the cost of services from American technology companies.DeepSeek worries wiped over a trillion dollars from market value of some of the biggest US companies in semiconductor, power and infrastructure sectors. Nvidia alone lost about 17% or close to $593 billion in market value, a record one-day loss for any company.The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is publishing notice of the Secretary of Homeland Security’s issuance of an order (1) excluding information technology products and services developed by Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co, Ltd (DeepSeek), to include affiliated entities as defined in applicable regulations, from federal civilian agency procurements; and, (2) removing all DeepSeek and DeepSeek-affiliate products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations, from civilian agency information technology.Earlier this month, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said that it will vote on October 29 to bar all Chinese labs from testing electronic devices such as smartphones, cameras and computers for use ‌in the US, widening a previous action targeting Beijing. The FCC said it will prohibit test labs and certification bodies in countries including China that deny reciprocal treatment to US-based test labs. In ⁠2025, the FCC banned testing of US electronics by labs owned or controlled by the Chinese government, and several dozen labs were barred.FCC Chair Brendan Carr had then said that 82% of electronics were tested in China, which does not have an agreement with ​the US. But the agency said this year that a substantial majority of China-based test labs were still ​testing US electronics. "Less than 4% of all electronic devices are tested in labs located inside the US," Carr said, adding the FCC will "insist on fair and reciprocal treatment in international commerce. "
Article Summary: US government bans Chinese AI company DeepSeek that had wiped more than $1 trillion from Wall Street in less than 2 hours. In an order, DHS has banned US civilian agency IT systems from using any DeepSeeks AI model. The US government is also banning acquisition of products and third-party services developed using DeepSeeker technology by US civilian government agencies.

Article Title: America's largest bank CEO Jamie Dimon makes it clear at earnings call that not giving AI Agents access to bank's data; calls it too risky for clients and JPMorgan
Article Text:
America's largest bank CEO Jamie Dimon makes it clear at earnings call that not giving AI Agents access to bank's data; calls it too risky for clients and JPMorgan

Bank blocks AI agents from taking actions confirms JPMorgan

‘Liability transfer’

Defensive move:

Smart Cash

Why banks are nervous

Jamie Dimon the CEO of America's largest bank JPMorgan Chase has made it clear that the bank will not allow external artificial intelligence agents to access customer accounts and carry out actions on the behalf of users, warning that the technology presently poses significant risks for both customers and bank. According to a report by CNBC, speaking during the bank’s third-quarter earnings call, Dimon said JPMorgan Chase is taking a cautious approach as technology companies including Meta roll out increasingly autonomous AI assistants. "We're not going to allow just any ... outside agent to come in inside the company, because it's just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan," Dimon told analysts. Dimon further added that the possibility of large numbers of autonomous agents interacting with banking systems raises security concerns. "You don't want rogue agents, and it could be thousands of them," Dimon saidA JPMorgan spokesperson confirmed to CNBC that the bank currently prevents external AI agents from operating customer accounts. According to the bank, third parties are not permitted to gain access by using customers' banking credentials and logging in on their behalf.While AI agents can access some account information in a read-only format through open banking providers and data connectors, they cannot carry out transactions such as sending money, moving funds or paying bills.The bank said it supports customer-authorised data sharing through open banking services and is working toward enabling agentic connections securely, but has not provided a timeline for allowing third-party AI agents to directly interact with customer accounts.Dimon said JPMorgan is using AI agents internally and plans to deploy them in customer-facing applications. He said the bank’s approach is not about being for or against the technology, but about making sure it serves customers safely. He also drew a line on liability when customers authorize outside agents to act for them. “If people are using them, they should understand the risk,” Dimon said. “They should understand there’s a liability transfer. ”In recent weeks, JPMorgan began a targeted pilot of its own AI tool, Smart Cash, Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Barnum said Tuesday. It aims to predict a user’s cash flow and move funds to maximize yield. That would appear to be a defensive move against external agents.Personal AI agents have gained mainstream popularity in recent months as models gain more autonomy, such as the ability to cancel subscriptions or use credit cards for a user. Instinct, a text-message-based digital concierge, launched earlier this year on an invitation-only basis. Its maker, San Francisco-based Spear Street Technology, was founded last year and reached a $10 billion valuation last month.In September, bank stocks fell after Meta’s Muse agent topped app download charts soon after its unveiling. Investors feared consumers would use agents to move funds from low-yielding accounts to higher-yielding ones. Weeks later, OpenAI released its own agent, Dots.Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok and others have pointed to the risks such agents pose to cheap bank deposits. That risk would be limited, though, if agents are not allowed to operate freely in customers’ accounts.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon says AI agents are 'too risky' for clients and the bank. JPMorgan is using AI agents internally and plans to deploy them in customer-facing applications. The bank supports customer-authorised data sharing through open banking services and is working toward enabling agentic connections.

Article Title: Google's ex-CEO Eric Schmidt backed Anthropic in 2021 with tens of millions; ahead of IPO, his stake may be worth...
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt's idea of a top programmer goes to bed at 7 PM

Eric Schmidt bought into Anthropic before Google did

Anthropic IPO valuation 'has slipped from the $2 trillion mark'

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt is set for one of the biggest personal paydays from Anthropic’s upcoming IPO. He owns about 1% of the Claude maker, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The stake goes back to a personal investment of tens of millions of dollars that Schmidt made in the AI startup’s Series A round in 2021.The timing is what makes the number stand out. Investors have been discussing a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion for Anthropic ahead of its share sale. At 1%, Schmidt’s holding would be worth somewhere between $15 billion and $20 billion. There is one open question, though. Bloomberg says it is unclear whether he has sold any part of his stake since that first cheque.Anthropic was only a few months old when Schmidt came in. Dario and Daniela Amodei had left OpenAI with a small group of researchers and raised $124 million in a Series A round in May 2021. Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn led the round, with Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz and Schmidt joining him. Secondary market data puts the post-money valuation of that round at about $623 million.Google arrived much later. In late 2022, the search giant reportedly paid around $300 million for roughly 10% of Anthropic, which valued the company at about $3 billion, nearly five times the Series A price.Schmidt, who ran Google from 2001 to 2011 and stayed on as Alphabet’s executive chairman until 2018, had placed his bet about a year and a half before his old company.Not every early backer was as lucky. Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX and Alameda Research put $500 million into Anthropic for a stake of about 8%. After FTX collapsed, its bankruptcy estate sold the entire holding in 2024 for roughly $1.3 billion to repay creditors.Anthropic confidentially submitted its draft IPO papers to the US Securities and Exchange Commission on June 1. A public filing could come as early as October 26, with the listing expected in mid-November, as per reports.The company’s revenue has grown fast. At an investor day last week, Anthropic said its third-quarter revenue rose 45% from the previous quarter to $16.8 billion, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis. For context, the company made nearly $4.6 billion in revenue in all of 2025.Some investors still left that meeting talking about a valuation closer to $1.5 trillion, below the roughly $2 trillion many had expected. Their main worry was slowing growth, since revenue had more than doubled between the first and second quarters this year.Even at the lower end of that range, a single cheque written in 2021 could turn into one of the largest individual windfalls of the entire offering. That depends on Schmidt having held on to all of it.
Article Summary: Anthropic's IPO valuation 'has slipped from the $2 trillion mark' Schmidt made a personal investment of tens of millions of dollars in the AI startup’s Series A round in 2021. It is unclear whether he has sold any part of his stake since that first cheque.

Article Title: As Apple becomes the first company to join Nvidia in $5 trillion club, here's the big 'iPhone message' from investors
Article Text:
The investor message: confidence despite cost pressure

Tim Cook’s record

AI remains the challenge

OpenAI threat and legal fight

Apple has become the second company after Nvidia to close with a market value above $5 trillion, underscoring investors’ continued faith in the iPhone maker despite the growing conversion over increasing hardware costs, AI competition and slowing growth. According to a report by Wall Street Journal, Apple ended trading a market capitalisation of about $5.005 trillion, making the first time the company has finished a trading session above the $5 trillion threshold. The milestone caps the tenure of former CEO Tim Cook, who oversaw a 13-fold increase in Apple’s market value during his 15 years at the helm. While, the rise of Nvidia has been fuelled by the AI boom and massive data centre sending, Apple’s ascent reflects something different: investor confidence in the resilience of its ecosystem and, most importantly, the willingness of iPhone users to continue paying more for Apple devices.Investors are so confident in Apple’s business that they have pushed up its shares even as big cost increases threaten profit margins. The cost of memory and storage chips inside iPhones, Macs and iPads has soared because data-center demand has caused shortages. Apple has responded by raising prices across its device lineup, including for older iPhone models that would typically get a price cut.In theory, that could hurt Apple, since buyers might wait longer to upgrade.Yet Apple shares have jumped 25% since the first wave of price increases.Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan said investors believe Apple’s customers will pay the higher prices, letting the company earn as much or more in total profit even if margins fall. He added that the new foldable iPhone Duo is likely to be popular and that the new Siri AI should prompt upgrades.Cook’s act will be tough to follow. During his 15-year tenure as CEO, which ended Aug. 31, Apple’s market capitalization grew 13-fold. The company nearly quadrupled its annual iPhone sales. Its services business grew from $10 billion a year to more than $100 billion. The Apple Watch and AirPods, which he launched, together generate more than $30 billion a year. Apple also returned more than $1 trillion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends.Apple shares trade at a premium to the S&P 500 even though its revenue is growing more slowly than the index average. Analysts say that is because investors see the shares as safe and the business as predictable. A key to that has been limited capital spending, which boosts returns and lowers risk. That has been especially clear during the AI build-out, when big tech rivals have rushed to spend huge sums on data centers while Apple has stuck to making devices and selling high-margin services for them.AI has long been seen as Apple’s Achilles’ heel. The company failed to build its own frontier model and let Siri fall far behind rivals. Apple hopes the new Siri AI, built with Google’s help and released this fall, will change that. It still lags rival AI systems in key respects, but it is built directly into the iPhone, which many people already use. Apple also has access to more personal data, which could in theory power compelling features, though new AI agents show the technology is advancing faster than Apple can keep up.Perhaps the biggest threat is OpenAI, which is planning a family of AI-powered devices and has poached hundreds of Apple employees to drive its hardware strategy. Apple sued OpenAI in July, alleging it stole trade secrets. OpenAI has said it is “not aware of any evidence that this complaint has merit.” In a new filing Wednesday, it alleged that Apple poached one of its own employees, who took confidential files with him. Apple said it found no evidence supporting that allegation.AI could be where Ternus makes his mark, the Journal said. He could usher in a new era of innovation and growth, or Apple could finally lose its status as the company that defines how people interact with computers.
Article Summary: Investors are so confident in Apple’s business that they have pushed up its shares even as big cost increases threaten profit margins. Apple shares trade at a premium to the S&P 500 even though its revenue is growing more slowly than the index average. Investors see the shares as safe and the business as predictable.

Article Title: Justice Department cracks on America's 'North Korean employees problem'; says: More than 70 US companies affected, shares scammers email IDs
Article Text:
How the scheme worked

FBI raids laptop farms

Arrests and charges

Texas raids

Email IDs made public

Changing tactics

The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced a coordinated crackdown on a North Korean remote IT worker scheme that allegedly infiltrated dozens of American companies using stolen identities, warning businesses about a growing threat that generated millions of dollars for Pyongyang. More than 70 US companies were affected by the operation, according to the department. The action includes criminal charges against multiple suspects, two arrests, searches of dozens of suspected "laptop farms" and the seizure of approximately 187 laptops and related devices used to help North Korean operatives obtain remote jobs at US companies.According to an indictment unsealed in the Northern District of Ohio, North Korean workers got remote jobs at US companies from 2019 to around July 2025. They used stolen or fabricated identity documents, plus VPNs and proxy infrastructure, to appear to be U.S.-based employees.U.S.-based facilitators hosted the laptops that victim companies issued to these “employees” at their homes, the so-called laptop farms. They set up the machines, installed remote-access software and transferred the earnings to accounts controlled by North Korea.The scheme generated about $3 million in revenue, believed to have been sent to sanctioned North Korean entities.Victims included companies in health care, communications, cyber support, retail and manufacturing across Ohio, 16 other states and Washington, D.C.As part of the operation, the FBI executed searches at more than 40 locations in Texas believed to be connected to "laptop farms" used by North Korean workers. Investigators seized approximately 187 laptops and remote-access devices that allegedly enabled the fraud. The DOJ said the activity has been linked to a threat group known as "Famous Chollima," which has previously been associated with North Korean IT worker operationsTwo US nationals, Michael James Bostelle of Pennsylvania and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo of Texas, were arrested on charges of wire fraud, money laundering and identity theft. The indictment also names 10 China-based defendants, with two more under seal. The FBI said 14 people in total face charges.From Sept. 21 to Sept. 25, the FBI searched more than 40 residences in Texas in what it calls Operation Lonestar Roundup. Agents seized about 187 laptops and KVM devices. Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike identified the group as “Famous Chollima.”“Every laptop farm we dismantle shuts down a revenue stream that the North Korean government relies on to fund weapons programs,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould of the Northern District of Texas.The department published 11 email addresses it says the operatives used and urged employers to add them to their screening indicators:Bright.star.me208@gmail.comMerrttank.bz@gmail.comrandyryang@gmail.commichaelb860102@gmail.comassassinki211@gmail.comdev.jerryyang@gmail.comdenis.turgenev2021@gmail.comyesiree.cano825@gmail.comthomasdenzelbrown@gmail.comanthonyortega4592@gmail.comtyler.j.palmi38@gmail.comThe FBI issued a public service announcement with guidance for companies. It warns that North Korean workers increasingly recruit American facilitators to get around better detection. They give those facilitators a wider range of tasks and sometimes subcontract whole jobs to third-party foreign nationals. Some have also committed data extortion and stolen sensitive company data.A 2022 advisory said individual North Korean IT workers can earn up to $300,000 a year. The State Department is offering rewards of up to $5 million for information that helps disrupt North Korea’s illicit financial activities.The department noted that the court filings contain allegations, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.
Article Summary: More than 70 US companies were affected by the operation, according to the department. The action includes criminal charges against multiple suspects, two arrests, searches of dozens of suspected "laptop farms" and the seizure of 187 laptops and related devices. The DOJ said the activity has been linked to a threat group known as "Famous Chollima"

Article Title: World’s most valuable memory chip maker to US: Accept this 'China condition' if you want us to build factories in America
Article Text:
Representative Image. Credit: SK Hynix

Why SK Hynix wants US approval for its China facility

"The installation of equipment for Mod B is being carried out in close consultation with and under authorisation from the US government."

"No capacity expansion is being sought for the Dalian Mod B, which was completed in 2023."

US export restrictions complicate SK Hynix’s plans

"Biden-era loophole."

SK Hynix’s plans for a US factory

NAND memory market drives expansion plans

SK Hynix is reportedly seeking US approval to expand its China operations. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, the South Korean memory chipmaker wants Washington’s permission to export additional US-made semiconductor manufacturing equipment to its Dalian facility in China. The report cited two people familiar with the matter, who said SK Hynix has made this a condition for funding its planned investment in American manufacturing.The report claims that the company’s US unit, Solidigm, is seeking an export licence to install equipment for producing NAND flash memory chips in unused space at the Chinese site. As per the report, the company is linking its plans for a new NAND factory in the US to its ability to increase production in China.The development comes as the Trump administration pushes foreign semiconductor companies to establish manufacturing facilities in America, while Washington continues to restrict China’s access to advanced chipmaking technology.Solidigm wants to install additional equipment at SK Hynix’s Dalian facility to manufacture NAND flash memory chips. These chips power solid-state drives (SSDs), which are increasingly important for data centres supporting artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing workloads.The Dalian facility already uses semiconductor manufacturing equipment supplied by US companies, including Lam Research, Applied Materials and KLA. However, Solidigm needs additional authorisation to purchase and install more US-made equipment at the site.The report cited one person familiar with the matter, who said the company believes increasing production in China would help Solidigm finance a NAND manufacturing facility in the US. It would also help pave the way for expanding production capacity in America.In a statement to Reuters, SK Hynix said,The company added,Solidigm declined to comment, while the US Department of Commerce did not respond to a request for comment.The request comes as Washington works to limit China’s access to semiconductor manufacturing technology. The US government has imposed export restrictions on chipmaking equipment to slow Beijing’s development of advanced semiconductors used in AI and military applications.Last year, the US Department of Commerce revoked authorisations that had allowed SK Hynix and Samsung to obtain US equipment for their Chinese factories without applying for individual licences. The department described the previous arrangements as aInstead, the government said it would issue export licences allowing the companies to operate their existing Chinese facilities, while signalling that it did not expect to approve applications for capacity expansion or technology upgrades.In December 2025, the department issued a licence for SK Hynix’s Dalian plant for 2026 but restricted the amount of equipment that could be exported. One source said the company has not yet been approved for more US-made equipment and technology for 2027.Mod B is a manufacturing facility in Dalian, built in 2023. Even after the memory market went into the doldrums, the equipment was not installed.The proposed American NAND factory is part of SK Hynix’s broader efforts to expand its manufacturing presence in the US. Reuters reported last month that Solidigm was considering building a NAND flash memory factory in the country.The company is also reportedly in talks with Intel to lease part of its planned chipmaking facility in Ohio. Separately, SK Hynix has broken ground on an advanced packaging plant in Indiana focused on high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which is used in AI systems.Building semiconductor fabrication plants, commonly called fabs, requires billions of dollars and can take several years. Another source said that Solidigm is also weighing an initial public offering (IPO) as early as next year, which could provide additional funding for its US factory plans.SK Hynix’s request comes after the NAND market has recovered from a previous downturn and struggled with supply constraints. Walt Coon, memory industry expert at TechInsights, said NAND pricing has surged sevenfold since mid-2023 and the market is likely to remain tight over the next few years.The company is one of the two leading global suppliers of NAND flash memory, alongside Samsung Electronics. However, China's YMTC moved up to third place in the second quarter of 2026, according to Counterpoint Research.
Article Summary: SK Hynix is reportedly seeking US approval to expand its China operations. The South Korean memory chipmaker wants Washington’s permission to export additional US-made semiconductor manufacturing equipment to its Dalian facility. The request comes as Washington works to limit China's access to semiconductor technology.

Article Title: Beyond the Strait: Gulf looks for an escape route from Hormuz
Article Text:
Vessels at the Strait of Hormuz (representational image)

$1.4 trillion infrastructure pipeline

Gulf remains attractive to investors despite war

The Middle East conflict has put the world’s energy lifeline, the Strait of Hormuz, in a chokehold.But the Gulf might be looking for an escape route.Over the next five years, countries in the region could invest in alternative logistics corridors and energy pipelines to loosen their dependence on the strategic waterway and keep oil and gas flowing, HSBC group chief executive Georges Elhedery said on Tuesday.The conflict has exposed the risks of depending on the strategic waterway, which previously carried a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade. Gulf nations are now being pushed to direct resources towards developing energy pipelines connecting production centres to ports, potentially allowing shipments to bypass the strait.Speaking at the HSBC Future Forum in Dubai, Elhedery said the region would be able to recover from the conflict and continue growing, but that doing so would require substantial investment."We do see this region being able to recover and then continue growing. It will mean a lot of investment," the bank CEO said."Of course, we do wish and hope to see a resolution to the conflict ... But Hormuz, probably in five years' time, may become redundant," he added.The shift towards alternative routes comes as the Middle East, North Africa and Turkey have a substantial pipeline of infrastructure projects that could attract investment.According to an HSBC report published on Monday, citing data from Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform MEED, the regions are offering $872 billion in individual project packages. These form part of a wider $1.4 trillion pipeline of infrastructure projects that have been planned but not yet awarded.The investment pipeline comes as Gulf countries consider ways to limit the disruption caused by the conflict and strengthen their ability to move energy supplies through routes other than the Strait of Hormuz.Despite the conflict, business leaders and institutional investors continue to view the Gulf as an attractive destination for investment.A recent HSBC survey of more than 1,600 business leaders and around 820 global institutional investors found that respondents still considered the region an appealing investment hub.However, the economic outlook for the wider region has weakened. After recording growth of 3.3% in 2025, the Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan region is expected to contract by 1.3% this year because of the war, according to a World Bank forecast issued last week.The contraction is expected to be followed by a strong but uneven recovery in 2027.Elhedery was among the global financiers expected to attend Saudi Arabia's flagship investment conference next week. The event was postponed until 2027 on Monday following deadly strikes in Riyadh by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis.
Article Summary: Gulf countries could invest in alternative logistics corridors and energy pipelines to loosen their dependence on the strategic waterway. The shift towards alternative routes comes as the Middle East, North Africa and Turkey have a substantial pipeline of infrastructure projects. Despite the conflict, business leaders and institutional investors continue to view the Gulf as an attractive destination for investment.

Delhi weather tomorrow

IMD's latest forecast

Article Title: A 3-hour peak-hour drive from Sarai Kale Khan to Sohna and Palwal took 45 minutes during trials, final stretch of Delhi-Faridabad expressway corridor completed
Article Text:
South Delhi MP Ramvir Singh Bidhuri announced that the new expressway corridor is nearing completion and will enhance connectivity. (File pic)





NEW DELHI: A journey from Sarai Kale Khan to Sohna and Palwal that usually takes around three hours during peak traffic was completed in 40-45 minutes during trial runs of a new expressway corridor, South Delhi MP Ramvir Singh Bidhuri said on Monday, announcing the completion of its final stretch.Sources indicated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi may inaugurate the corridor later this year.Bidhuri, along with Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, recently inspected the stretch while the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was conducting load testing and other technical evaluations.Once fully operational, the corridor is expected to improve connectivity between Delhi and key destinations in Haryana, including Faridabad, Sohna and Palwal. It will connect Sarai Kale Khan with Jaitpur and Meethapur before extending towards Faridabad and linking up with the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal (KMP) Expressway and the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway network.The DND-Faridabad-Sohna Access Controlled Highway (NH-148A) is 59km long, while the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway stretch between the DND Flyway and Jaitpur covers another 9km. The DND-Jaitpur section provides a direct link from Delhi to the wider expressway network, while adjoining sections connect commuters to Faridabad and the KMP Expressway.The new corridor is expected to offer an alternative to existing routes used by commuters travelling from Delhi to Faridabad and other parts of southern Haryana.“This would be a major relief for the South Delhi constituency as the new corridor would help ease congestion at Ashram Chowk, Kalindi Kunj and along Mathura Road, besides reducing travel time and fuel consumption,” Bidhuri said. He added that the completion of the final stretch would provide a major boost to commuters travelling towards southern Haryana.Traffic heading towards Faridabad, Ballabhgarh and Sohna is expected to shift to the expressway, easing pressure on the congested Ring Road and Mathura Road. According to Bidhuri, the journey from the DND Flyway to Faridabad could take around 20 minutes, compared with the current 30 minutes required to cover the Ashram-Badarpur border section.Delhi stretch on trial, Haryana section operationalThe corridor comprises sections at different stages of operation. The 9km Delhi stretch between the DND Flyway and Jaitpur has opened on a trial basis. It is currently toll-free, with a speed limit of 40kmph, while NHAI monitors traffic movement.The 50km Haryana section, extending from Jaitpur towards Sohna and the KMP Expressway, has moved beyond the trial phase and is operational, with toll collection in place.The completion of the final stretch is expected to improve connectivity between Delhi and southern Haryana, although the extent of the time savings for commuters will depend on traffic conditions and the corridor's operational arrangements.
Article Summary: A journey from Sarai Kale Khan to Sohna and Palwal was completed in 40-45 minutes during trial runs. South Delhi MP Ramvir Singh Bidhuri announced the completion of its final stretch. The corridor is expected to improve connectivity between Delhi and key destinations in Haryana.
